label: Loud noise
summary: Generators, chainsaws, grinders, cut-off saws, compressors and engines damage hearing a little at a time, without pain, and the damage is permanent. Ringing or dull hearing after work is the warning.
signs: You have to shout to be heard by someone close by
Ringing or buzzing in your ears afterwards
Sounds seem muffled after the noise stops
do: Wear earplugs or earmuffs around loud machines, and both together for the loudest jobs
Fit foam plugs properly: roll them thin, pull the ear up and back, push them in and hold until they expand
Put generators and compressors away from where people work and sleep, behind something solid
Take breaks away from the noise
dont: Don’t rely on cotton wool or fingers in your ears for more than a moment
Don’t treat ringing that fades as harmless
ppe: Foam earplugs, fitted properly, or earmuffs
Plugs and muffs together for chainsaws, cut-off saws and similar
firstAid: There is no fix for noise damage once it’s done; ringing that fades still means some harm. Keep away from loud noise and protect what hearing is left
